source_document.body:
In 2027, changing expectations from global shippers will continue to shape the logistics industry.
What’s Related
Shippers will increasingly expect logistics providers to move beyond transactional services—anticipating problems, answering questions before issues escalate and offering strategic guidance as trade conditions change.
They will look for technology that improves supply chain visibility , efficiency and resilience while making it easier to work with their logistics providers. At the same time, they will continue to value access to experienced professionals who can provide insight and judgment when situations become complex.
This combination of technology-enabled speed and intelligence with human expertise will shape freight forwarding and customs brokerage in 2027.
RELATED STORIES: Top Supply Chain Technology Trends for 2026 | Transportation and Logistics Trends for 2026
2027 trends to watch
Reliable data becomes foundational — Companies will prioritize accurate, connected data and technology that provides the flexibility and resilience to respond quickly to changing conditions.
The freight forwarder becomes a strategic advisor — Forwarders will increasingly help shippers identify alternatives, understand cost and service trade-offs, anticipate disruptions and reduce risk.
AI moves into practical workflows — AI will become increasingly embedded in everyday activities such as extracting shipment data from documents, supporting tariff classification research, identifying missing information, preparing freight rate quotes and prioritizing operational exceptions.
AI-ready workforces become essential — Logistics organizations will need to prepare employees to work effectively with AI while maintaining appropriate human oversight.
Connected systems become a requirement — Data integrations between logistics providers, shippers, customs brokers and other supply chain partners will become increasingly important for efficiency and visibility.
Technology takes on a greater role in Customs Compliance — As regulatory requirements and trade complexity increase, technology will become increasingly important for managing compliance processes, improving data accuracy and supporting customs professionals.
Exception management becomes more proactive — Technology will help teams identify potential disruptions earlier and focus human attention where intervention is most needed.
Visibility evolves into actionable intelligence — Shippers will expect technology to do more than report what is happening; they will want insights that help them determine what to do next.
Flexibility becomes a competitive requirement — Forwarders will need technology, processes and operating models that can adapt as trade regulations, tariffs, capacity and customer requirements change.
Human expertise remains a differentiator — As more routine activities become automated , experienced logistics and customs professionals will play an increasingly important role in handling exceptions, interpreting complex situations and advising customers.
Freight forwarders and customs brokers that combine connected technology, reliable data, practical AI and knowledgeable teams will be better positioned to help shippers navigate continued trade and supply chain volatility in 2027.
